templateName: SAM 3D Objects (Meta): print-ready, with a base
description: SAM 3D Objects with the print gate closed (a failing check writes no mesh) and a printed base added under the model. For a model that goes straight to a 3D printer.
inputInstructions:
Reconstructs a textured 3D mesh from one photo using Meta SAM 3D Objects, which segments the subject in place and is the most tolerant of cluttered, real-world scenes. Licensed under the Meta SAM License, which carries trade-control terms and requires that redistribution stay under the same licence. A run typically takes 3 to 8 minutes and needs about 24 GB of GPU memory.

SAM 3D field: Seed makes a run repeatable. The model exposes no sampling or resolution knobs — its reconstruction quality comes from the segmentation it performs itself, so the photo and the background-removal choice are what move the result.

All options are set on this form; the values you choose are the only ones the run uses. Leaving a field alone applies the default shown beside it.

Stages this model runs: image cleanup prepares the photo, the generate stage segments the subject and reconstructs it with per-vertex colour carried on the mesh, and mesh cleanup repairs and rescales while carrying that colour across. There is no separate texture stage and no projection stage -- the colour arrives with the geometry.

Print readiness: with Mesh cleanup on, the generated mesh is decimated, repaired and rescaled, then checked for printability — watertight, no non-manifold edges or vertices, positive volume, no broken faces. failClosed rejects the run and writes no mesh when any check fails, and still writes the gate report so the failure is legible. bestEffort writes every output and records the check results in the report. With Mesh cleanup off the mesh is returned exactly as the model generated it and is not guaranteed to be printable.

FORM. Each field is labelled with the stage that reads it, in the order a run executes them: [1 Input] prepares the photographs, [2 Generate] is this template's model, [3 Cleanup] repairs the mesh and brings it to the face count, [4 Colour] projects the photograph onto it, [5 Print] sizes it, adds print features and applies the print gate, and [6 Output] chooses the formats and reports. A template shows only the stages its model uses.

tagSchema.label: [1 Input] Image cleanup
tagSchema.description: auto segments the subject from its background and frames it for the selected model. skip takes the image as already segmented and hands it to the model exactly as supplied, which removes that stage's time and cost -- choose it when the input is known to be a clean cutout. Skipping also bypasses framing, because without a mask there is no way to locate the subject.

tagSchema.label: [1 Input] Background removal
tagSchema.description: Segmentation model used to isolate the subject before reconstruction. Choose none when the photo already has a clean background. rembg, birefnet and rmbg2 decide for themselves which object the photo is of, so on a frame holding several they pick one and there is no way to ask for another; sam segments whatever SAM prompt points at. sam returns a hard-edged mask with no soft alpha through hair, so it is the choice for selecting an object rather than for a difficult edge.

tagSchema.label: [1 Input] SAM prompt
tagSchema.description: Where to look, used only when Background removal is sam. centre takes the middle of the frame, which is where a framed subject sits. x,y names a point and x0,y0,x1,y1 a box, given as fractions of the image between 0 and 1 rather than as pixels so one value holds at any resolution. A point asks for the object there; a box also bounds the answer, which is the stronger prompt where objects overlap.

tagSchema.label: [1 Input] Framing ratio
tagSchema.description: Fraction of the frame the subject is scaled to fill before reconstruction. auto uses the framing the selected model expects and is the right choice unless you are comparing runs. A lower value leaves more margin around the subject; a higher value gives the model more pixels on it but crops closer to its edges.

tagSchema.label: [1 Input] Framing background
tagSchema.description: Flat colour composited behind the subject before reconstruction. The subject is always cropped and scaled to the framing ratio; this setting decides only what sits behind it. auto uses the background the selected model was trained against. none composites nothing and keeps the alpha channel, which a model that reads alpha as an object mask requires.

tagSchema.label: [2 Generate] Seed
tagSchema.description: Random seed for the reconstruction. The same seed on the same photo and settings reproduces the same mesh; change it to get a different interpretation of an ambiguous subject. Costs no extra run time.

tagSchema.label: [2 Generate] Solid interior
tagSchema.description: Fill the reconstruction's interior before the mesh is extracted. Off, the raw mesh is a closed outer shell with a second, inward-facing wall one voxel inside it, sealing a void of about a third of the object's volume that the cleanup ladder then has to resolve. On, the enclosed volume reads as solid and only the outer surface is extracted. Costs a few seconds.

tagSchema.label: [3 Cleanup] Mesh cleanup
tagSchema.description: Run the print-readiness cleanup (decimate, repair, rescale, gate). Set false to return the mesh exactly as generated, which is not guaranteed to be printable.

tagSchema.label: [3 Cleanup] Mesh repair ladder
tagSchema.description: Which repair backends the print-readiness cleanup may walk, least to most invasive. The full ladder gives the best chance of a watertight, printable result; the permissive-only option limits the run to trimesh (MIT) and manifold3d (Apache-2.0) and excludes the GPL-3.0 backends. Applies only when Mesh cleanup is on.

tagSchema.label: [3 Cleanup] Minimum volume retained by a repair
tagSchema.description: Fraction of the mesh's original volume a repair step must leave behind for its result to be kept. The print-readiness gate measures printability, not likeness, so a step that discards most of the model produces something trivially watertight and useless; a repair falling below this floor is discarded and the ladder continues without it. Lower the floor to allow more aggressive repair, or set 0 to accept any result.

tagSchema.label: [3 Cleanup] Largest hole the repair may close (edges)
tagSchema.description: Boundary size, in edges, of the largest hole the pymeshlab repair rung will close. The library's own default is 30 and it leaves anything wider open without reporting it, which is why a run could finish with the rung applied and still fail the gate. Printing needs a closed surface, so the generous default is usually right; lower it when a hole is part of the subject -- the opening of a cup, say -- and you would rather keep the shape than close it. 0 closes nothing.

tagSchema.label: [3 Cleanup] Target face count
tagSchema.description: Face budget the cleaned mesh is decimated to. 0 leaves the generated face count untouched.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Target size (mm)
tagSchema.description: Longest-edge size the mesh is rescaled to, in millimetres. 0 leaves the model's own scale untouched.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Print features
tagSchema.description: Parametric geometry added to the finished mesh for printing. loop adds a hanging ring at the top of the model,; base adds a flat-bottomed cylinder underneath, so the model stands and the slicer gets a stable first layer. The dimensions below are millimetres of the printed object and are applied after the rescale, so set Target size (mm) as well — with it left at 0 the model keeps its own arbitrary scale and a millimetre dimension has no fixed meaning.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] How the feature is attached
tagSchema.description: A boolean union fuses the feature into one solid but discards the mesh's texture entirely, so it cannot be used on a colour print. concat keeps the texture and leaves the feature as a second closed shell overlapping the model, which slicers resolve when they fill. auto chooses per mesh — concat when the mesh carries a texture, union when it is geometry-only and so has no colour to lose — and is the right choice unless you are comparing runs. The join used and the resulting body count are recorded in the run report, because the print gate accepts both.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Print feature colour
tagSchema.description: Flat colour the added geometry is given, as #RRGGBB, so a colour print shows a deliberate solid-coloured fitting. Without its own colour the feature samples whatever part of the model's texture its unwrap lands on and prints as a smear of the subject's colours. Has no effect when the join fuses to a single solid, which carries no texture.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Loop hole diameter (mm)
tagSchema.description: Clear opening a ring has to pass through, in millimetres. 0 sizes the loop to the model's own height.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Loop thickness (mm)
tagSchema.description: Thickness of the loop's tube, in millimetres. 0 uses a fraction of the hole diameter. Must stay below the hole diameter, or the opening closes and the loop cannot be threaded.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Base diameter (mm)
tagSchema.description: Diameter of the stand base, in millimetres. 0 sizes it slightly wider than the model's own footprint.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Base height (mm)
tagSchema.description: Height of the stand base, in millimetres. 0 uses a fraction of the model's own height.

tagSchema.label: [5 Print] Print gate policy
tagSchema.description: What happens when a print-readiness check fails. failClosed writes no mesh, only the gate report; bestEffort writes the outputs and records the failures.

tagSchema.label: [6 Output] Export formats
tagSchema.description: Which containers the finished mesh is written as. glb carries geometry and texture in one file and is what the VAMS viewer reads; obj writes the texture as a separate file set; stl is geometry only and is the 3D-printing format. Choose stl alone for a print-only run, or glb alone for a viewer-only preview.

tagSchema.label: [6 Output] Benchmark report
tagSchema.description: Records per-stage timings and the hardware the run landed on into the run report, so model, segmentation path and quality settings can be compared on speed and cost as well as on the mesh. Off by default; it adds no GPU work but does add detail to the report.

tagSchema.label: [6 Output] Pass the input photographs on
tagSchema.description: true copies the input photograph(s) into this run's outputs beside the mesh, so a later pipeline in the same workflow receives them together with the mesh. A workflow's second step is handed only the first step's outputs, so a reconstruct-then-refine workflow needs this on its first step. false leaves the outputs as the mesh, its formats and the reports.
